message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# Copyright The SimpleKernel Contributors

name: build

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  release:
    types: [published]

# Cancel in-progress runs for the same branch/PR
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  # PR: 3 runs for speed; push/release: 10 runs for stability
  SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 3 || 10 }}

jobs:
  build-riscv64:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/simple-xx/simplekernel-dev:latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Shallow submodule init
        run: |
          git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
          git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1

      - name: Cache CMake build (riscv64)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: build_riscv64/
          key: cmake-riscv64-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('CMakeLists.txt', 'cmake/**', 'src/**') }}
          restore-keys: |
            cmake-riscv64-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Configure & Build
        run: |
          cmake --preset=build_riscv64
          cmake --build build_riscv64 --target SimpleKernel docs

      - name: System Test
        run: |
          for i in $(seq 1 $SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS); do
            echo "=== riscv64 System Test Run $i/$SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS ==="
            timeout 300 cmake --build build_riscv64 --target system_test_run > /tmp/st_out_$i.txt 2>&1 || true
            cat /tmp/st_out_$i.txt
            if ! grep -q "RESULT: ALL TESTS PASSED" /tmp/st_out_$i.txt; then
              echo "riscv64 system test run $i/$SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS FAILED"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "riscv64 system test run $i/$SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS passed"
          done

      - name: Upload docs artifact
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: docs-html
          path: docs/html/
          retention-days: 1

  build-aarch64:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/simple-xx/simplekernel-dev:latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Shallow submodule init
        run: |
          git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
          git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1

      - name: Cache CMake build (aarch64)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: build_aarch64/
          key: cmake-aarch64-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('CMakeLists.txt', 'cmake/**', 'src/**') }}
          restore-keys: |
            cmake-aarch64-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Configure & Build
        run: |
          cmake --preset=build_aarch64 -DQEMU_NORMAL_WORLD_DEV_PATH=null -DQEMU_SECURE_WORLD_DEV_PATH=null
          cmake --build build_aarch64 --target SimpleKernel unit-test coverage

      - name: System Test
        run: |
          for i in $(seq 1 $SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS); do
            echo "=== aarch64 System Test Run $i/$SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS ==="
            timeout 300 cmake --build build_aarch64 --target system_test_run > /tmp/st_out_$i.txt 2>&1 || true
            cat /tmp/st_out_$i.txt
            if ! grep -q "RESULT: ALL TESTS PASSED" /tmp/st_out_$i.txt; then
              echo "aarch64 system test run $i/$SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS FAILED"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "aarch64 system test run $i/$SYSTEM_TEST_RUNS passed"
          done

      - name: Upload coverage reports to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: ${{ github.workspace }}/build_aarch64/coverage/coverage.info
          verbose: true

  publish:
    needs: [build-riscv64, build-aarch64]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Download docs artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: docs-html
          path: docs/html/

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: docs/html/",
  "rationale": "Added explicit job timeouts (timeout-minutes: 30) to both build jobs following the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern. The workflow currently relies on GitHub Actions' default 6-hour timeout, but historical runs complete in ~8-10 minutes. A 30-minute timeout provides ample headroom for kernel builds and system test runs (3 for PRs, 10 for pushes/releases, each with a 5-minute per-run timeout) while preventing runaway jobs from consuming excessive resources. This optimization is supported by experimental evidence showing ~27% elapsed time savings when adding custom timeouts to jobs without them. The workflow already has concurrency cancellation (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) and CMake build caching, so no changes needed for those patterns.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
message.reasoning:
Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence to determine what optimization can be applied.

The workflow is for a kernel project (SimpleKernel) that builds for two architectures (riscv64 and aarch64) and runs system tests. It already has:
1. Concurrency cancellation for superseded runs (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE)
2. CMake build caching for each architecture
3. Container-based builds

Looking at the evidence provided:
1. P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE - shows caching pip dependencies for Python projects
2. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT - shows adding timeout-minutes to jobs
3. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST - shows enabling fail-fast for matrix jobs
4. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE - shows adding concurrency cancellation (already present in workflow)
5. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE - shows caching Gradle dependencies

The workflow already has:
- Concurrency cancellation (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) - already implemented
- CMake build caching - already implemented for both architectures

What's missing? The workflow doesn't have explicit job timeouts. The system tests run with a 300-second (5-minute) timeout per run, but the jobs themselves don't have a timeout-minutes setting. Given that the workflow runs on ARM runners (ubuntu-24.04-arm) and does kernel builds + system tests, adding a custom timeout could prevent runaway jobs.

Looking at P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern:
- It adds `timeout-minutes` to jobs
- The evidence shows 26.8% elapsed savings in one experiment
- Preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists"
- Contraindications: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit"

The workflow has historical runs showing durations. Let me check the CI history:
- Runs take around 8-10 minutes (from created_at to updated_at)
- The jobs do kernel builds and system tests (3 runs for PR, 10 for push/release)

A reasonable timeout would be something like 30-45 minutes to allow for the build and all test runs while preventing stuck jobs.

Also, the workflow has two independent jobs (build-riscv64 and build-aarch64) that run in parallel. They don't use a matrix strategy, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST doesn't apply directly.

The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern is about caching dependency downloads, but this workflow uses a container with pre-installed dependencies (ghcr.io/simple-xx/simplekernel-dev:latest) and caches CMake build outputs, not dependencies.

Given the evidence, the most applicable optimization is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT - adding explicit job timeouts to prevent runaway builds. The workflow currently relies on the default 6-hour GitHub Actions timeout, but the actual runs complete in ~10 minutes. Adding a timeout of say 30 minutes would be safe and follow the pattern.

Let me check if there's evidence for this in the provided records. The experiment for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job that previously had none, with 26.8% elapsed savings.

For this workflow, I should add timeout-minutes to both build jobs. Given the system test runs (3 for PR, 10 for push/release) each with 300s timeout, plus build time, a 30-minute timeout seems reasonable.

Let me create the updated workflow with timeout-minutes added to both jobs.
